reason: The text demonstrates agency exercised by multiple groups beyond leadership. All Israel collectively gathers and participates in making David king (וַיִּקָּבְצ֧וּ כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל - 'all Israel gathered'). Individual mighty men—soldiers rather than leaders—perform autonomous military heroics: three men independently breach the Philistine camp to fetch water for David (וַיִּבְקְע֨וּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֜ה), Joab advances first to become commander, and Benaiah slays Egyptian warriors and a lion. These non-leaders make choices, take risks, and execute significant actions, directly contradicting the notion that only leaders possess agency.
